policydecision_details: The Government of Kenya is establishing 10 specialised 250-bed maternal and newborn health facilities across 10 counties to reduce preventable deaths. These facilities will integrate comprehensive services including antenatal care, labour, recovery, and neonatal intensive care. The project is supported by a KES 4.4 billion (USD 34 million) grant from the Amsons Group under the Mama na Mtoto Kwanza initiative. Additionally, KES 4 billion is being allocated through the Social Health Authority to support maternal deliveries at lower-level facilities. Groundbreaking for the new facilities is expected by September 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: Kenya is addressing high maternal and newborn mortality rates by targeting 26 counties that account for approximately 60 per cent of maternal deaths in the country. This initiative aligns with President William Ruto’s directive to prioritize maternal health and advance Universal Health Coverage. The project complements existing efforts like the 'Every Woman Every Newborn Everywhere' programme and follows World Health Organization benchmarks for specialized care.

policydecision_details: The government of Belarus has introduced new regulations for school nutrition effective September 1, 2026. Monetary norms for school food spending will increase by 5% and will be subject to automatic annual adjustments based on retail price changes. The policy introduces new meal structures, including a 'second breakfast' and 'afternoon snack', and reorganizes student age groups into three categories to better meet physiological needs. Additionally, the list of permitted food products has been expanded to include various semi-finished goods, and restrictions on certain items like lard and pates have been removed.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to improve the quality and nutritional standards of school meals in Belarus by aligning them with the physiological needs of different age groups and adjusting for inflation in food prices.
budget: 5% increase in monetary norms for food spending

policydecision_details: The Mozambican government is investing USD 15 million to modernize the Ressano Garcia border post. The project focuses on upgrading technological infrastructure, developing a road freight terminal, and implementing express lanes to improve border efficiency. It aims to reduce waiting times, lower logistical costs, and enhance the movement of goods between Mozambique and South Africa. Additionally, the initiative includes the digitalization of systems to improve information sharing, traceability, and the fight against smuggling.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Ressano Garcia border is a vital economic artery for Mozambique, particularly for trade with South Africa. Currently, the formation of long queues of trucks on the EN4 road causes significant economic losses, including increased fuel consumption, vehicle wear, and the risk of cargo deterioration. The modernization project is designed to address these constraints, improve the competitiveness of the Port of Maputo, and boost overall tax revenue collection.
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized companies, national suppliers, local communities, logistics and transport operators

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has reduced the maximum retail price of diesel by Sh5 per litre. Prices for super petrol and kerosene remain unchanged for the period between August 15 and September 14, 2026. This adjustment is part of the monthly review of petroleum prices mandated by the Petroleum Act, 2019. The government provided Sh938 million in stabilization support to cushion consumers from price fluctuations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The price adjustment follows a monthly review of petroleum prices based on changes in global petroleum costs, taxes, and government interventions. The review was conducted amid mixed trends in the average landed cost of imported petroleum products, with diesel and kerosene costs declining while super petrol costs rose.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: The Swiss government has introduced a temporary relaxation of import duties on silage maize to support livestock farmers facing severe drought conditions. From August 15 to October 31, 2026, maize for animal feed with a dry matter content of up to 60% can be imported into Switzerland free of charge. This measure aims to help farmers build adequate winter feed reserves following poor forage yields. Additionally, the government has lifted customs duties on hay and provided access to interest-free operating loans for farms facing liquidity issues.
contextoradditionalinfo: Switzerland has been experiencing severe drought conditions characterized by high temperatures and sparse rainfall, which have significantly reduced forage yields and increased feed prices. The Swiss Farmers’ Union proposed these measures to mitigate the impact of the drought on the agricultural sector and ensure the availability of animal feed.
decision_making_institution: Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Mozambican authorities have activated preventive response mechanisms in 26 districts identified as being at risk of drought. Specifically, 13 districts have reached the 'set' phase, which is classified as a severe risk level, triggering immediate intervention protocols. The government is monitoring these areas to mitigate the humanitarian impacts of the El Niño phenomenon. These measures aim to address potential food insecurity, water shortages, and health needs in the affected regions. The response is part of a broader effort to manage climate-related risks through March 2027.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Kenyan National Assembly has passed the Plant Protection Bill (National Bill No. 28 of 2025) to establish a modern legal and institutional framework for agricultural biosecurity. The legislation replaces the outdated Plant Protection Act, Cap. 324, to better address contemporary agricultural practices and international trade requirements. It formally designates the Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS) as the National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO). The bill shifts the national plant health system from reactive measures to a proactive, science-based approach to prevent the spread of plant pests.
contextoradditionalinfo: The existing Plant Protection Act, Cap. 324, was deemed inadequate by the Departmental Committee on Agriculture and Livestock due to its inability to address emerging technologies, modern agricultural practices, and evolving international phytosanitary standards. The new legislation aims to close enforcement gaps and reduce the risk of non-tariff barriers and export rejections, thereby protecting agricultural production and food security.

policydecision_details: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) has announced a commitment to strengthen financial support for key economic areas to foster high-quality development. This includes expanding domestic demand, promoting technological innovation, and providing targeted support for small and micro enterprises. The central bank continues to implement an accommodative monetary policy and optimize structural monetary policy tools. By the end of June 2026, loan growth in sectors such as technology, green finance, and the digital economy significantly outpaced total loan growth. The PBOC aims to maintain stable financial market operations and prevent systemic financial risks while managing exchange rate stability.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Commerce of China has announced the extension of anti-dumping measures on imports of single-mode optical fibers from India. These duties will remain in effect for an additional five-year period. This decision follows a recommendation from the Customs Tariff Commission. The measure is part of China's ongoing trade defense strategy regarding specific industrial imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is a continuation of existing trade defense instruments intended to protect domestic industries from what is perceived as dumped imports. The announcement also notes that China is simultaneously maintaining anti-dumping duties on solar-grade polysilicon from the US and South Korea and has initiated new investigations into other imports.
decision_making_institution: Customs Tariff Commission of the State Council
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Hungarian government has ordered the immediate construction of a submerged weir on the Danube near the Paks nuclear power plant to mitigate the impact of record-low water levels. As a temporary emergency measure, two 80-metre barges will be placed on standby and may be sunk in a controlled operation to maintain water levels for the plant's cooling system. The project aims to prevent a complete shutdown of the nuclear facility, which would cause significant economic damage. The government has classified this as a priority investment, with construction beginning immediately under the coordination of the Defence Administration Office.
contextoradditionalinfo: Prolonged low water levels in the Danube have threatened the operational capacity of the Paks nuclear power plant, which is critical for Hungary's energy security and economy. Previous lack of investment in contingency infrastructure, such as pumping stations, has left the plant vulnerable to these environmental conditions. The government is intervening to avoid a potential shutdown that would cost the state budget at least 50 billion forints per month.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Mozambican Cabinet approved the new Merchant Shipping and Related Activities Law and a new Maritime Transport Regulation to establish a modern legal framework for maritime operations. These measures aim to improve maritime safety, prevent marine pollution, and regulate the activities of shipowners and shipping companies. Additionally, the government created the Southern Integrated Development Agency (ADISUL) to coordinate socio-economic development in the southern provinces. The new regulations are expected to boost cabotage transport and reduce the costs of transporting goods, thereby lowering consumer prices.

The Fergana region of Uzbekistan has announced plans to invest USD 10 million in new cotton processing and knitwear production projects. This initiative aims to enhance the local value chain by shifting from raw material export to finished textile manufacturing. The project is expected to boost regional industrial capacity and create new employment opportunities within the textile sector. These investments are part of a broader strategy to modernize the agricultural processing infrastructure in the region.

The Bulgarian government has approved its Governance Program for 2026-2030, which outlines a long-term development framework for the country. The program focuses on restoring the rule of law, increasing institutional transparency, and dismantling corrupt governance models. It aims to modernize the economy by shifting from a model based on cheap labor and consumption to one driven by high-tech, export-oriented industries and increased productivity. The policy also includes specific commitments to improve healthcare, support for older people, and opportunities for youth.
contextoradditionalinfo: The program is based on the election platform of the ruling Progressive Bulgaria coalition and was adopted to translate campaign commitments into a concrete, long-term strategic plan. It seeks to align Bulgaria's living standards with those of developed European countries and rebuild public confidence in state institutions following a period of political instability.

policydecision_details: The Bulgarian Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation has announced a new funding procedure providing nearly USD 96 million to support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The program aims to facilitate the implementation of green technologies in production processes to foster a circular economy. Eligible businesses can receive grants ranging from 89,000 to 520,000 USD, with co-financing covering up to 70% of project costs. Applications are open until November 10, 2026, and must be submitted electronically through the national management information system.
contextoradditionalinfo: This initiative is part of the broader 'Competitiveness and Innovation in Enterprises' program, designed to encourage investments in environmentally friendly production methods. By supporting the adoption of green technologies, the government aims to improve resource efficiency and ensure compliance with European environmental standards. This follows previous similar procedures aimed at diversifying and adapting SMEs to the ongoing economic transition.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation

policydecision_details: The Latvian government has supported legislative amendments to expand the existing import ban on goods from Belarus and Russia. The current restrictions, which cover agricultural products and feed, will be extended to include a wider range of prepared food products. Specific items targeted include confectionery, sauces, soups, and beverages. The measure aims to create a legal basis for these broader import restrictions, though it will not affect transit through Latvia or deliveries to other EU countries.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Latvian Ministry of Agriculture is seeking to tighten trade restrictions on Belarus and Russia by expanding the scope of the current import ban to include processed food products. This move is part of a broader effort to restrict the entry of goods from these countries into the Latvian market.
commodity3: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: From 12 August, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) applies across the EU. The PPWR establishes a harmonised framework for packaging and packaging waste in the Single Market. The new rules mark a major step towards reducing packaging waste and lowering compliance costs for the packaging industry. They will also make the waste value chain more sustainable, helping to reduce the Union’s dependence on imports of virgin materials, strengthening the market for secondary raw materials, and supporting the EU’s transition to a competitive circular economy and climate neutrality by 2050.

The United States has pledged an additional $242 million to support Ebola response and preparedness efforts across East and Central Africa. This funding aims to strengthen health systems, enhance surveillance, and improve laboratory testing capabilities in countries at risk, including Kenya. The initiative focuses on containing the Bundibugyo virus disease by providing emergency response operations and critical medical supplies. Kenya is specifically targeted due to its role as a regional transport hub and its proximity to affected areas in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
contextoradditionalinfo: The funding is a response to the outbreak of the Bundibugyo virus, a form of Ebola, in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Because there is currently no approved vaccine for this specific strain, regional health authorities are prioritizing early detection, isolation, and infection prevention. Kenya's strategic position as a regional hub necessitates enhanced preparedness to prevent the cross-border spread of the disease.

policy_description: Establishment or modification of food stock
policydecision_details: The Kenyan government has announced plans to import one million 90-kilogram bags of maize to replenish strategic grain reserves. This measure is intended to mitigate an expected national maize shortfall of 5.4 million bags by the end of September 2026. The procurement may be executed through a government-to-government arrangement to stabilize supply. The government is also considering further interventions, including the potential release of existing reserves, if the supply gap widens.
policycategory: Establishment or modification of food stock

policydecision_details: China has announced a comprehensive ecological conservation plan for the 2026-2030 period aimed at enhancing ecosystem quality, stability, and resilience. The policy sets specific targets, including maintaining protected land areas at a minimum of 18 percent and increasing forest coverage to 25.8 percent. It also mandates raising the Ecological Quality Index to 86.5 and improving soil and water conservation rates to over 74 percent. These measures are designed to optimize ecological spatial configuration and strengthen biodiversity conservation nationwide.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of China's ongoing commitment to green modernization and sustainable development. It follows the introduction of the country's landmark Ecological and Environmental Code, which provides the necessary legal framework to support these long-term environmental protection goals.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Ecology and Environment, Ministry of Natural Resources

policydecision_details: The National Communications Institute of Mozambique (INCM) has launched the National Broadband and Coverage Planning Portal, a geospatial platform designed to monitor broadband coverage across the country. This interactive tool integrates statistical and geographic data to support evidence-based decision-making for the expansion of telecommunications infrastructure. By identifying areas with and without broadband access, the portal aims to guide public policy and investment more effectively. Additionally, it enables citizens to report coverage issues directly, fostering transparency and active participation in service improvement.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: State-owned company EGENCO has commissioned a 10 MW solar power plant in Salima, Malawi, as the first phase of a larger 50 MW renewable energy project. The project was financed through the utility's own resources at a cost of USD 13.55 million. This initiative is designed to be implemented in three stages to gradually increase solar capacity. The plant aims to diversify the national energy generation fleet, which currently relies heavily on hydropower. This development is part of a broader strategy to improve grid flexibility and reduce supply constraints.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The People's Bank of China has released a comprehensive reform and development plan for the 2026-2030 period aimed at strengthening the nation's financial sector. The plan focuses on advancing high-level financial opening-up, including the expansion of the renminbi's global use and the enhancement of the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System. It also outlines reforms to the domestic monetary policy framework to improve market-based interest rate and exchange-rate mechanisms. Furthermore, the policy emphasizes supporting the real economy through targeted financial services for innovation, green development, and inclusive finance. The central bank aims to mitigate systemic risks by expanding macro-prudential management and establishing robust monitoring systems.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Belarusian government has approved a draft agreement with Russia to establish operating rules for the Union State's common electricity market. This resolution follows the ratification of the treaty on the formation of a unified electricity market. The Ministry of Energy is mandated to sign these rules, which delegate management authority to the Ministry of Energy and the Ministry of Antimonopoly Regulation and Trade. This move aims to formalize the integration of energy markets between the two nations.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Generalitat Valenciana has approved a USD 77 million emergency aid package to support victims of the La Vall d’Uixó wildfire. The funding includes direct payments for individuals, support for local councils, and interest-free loans for affected businesses and farmers. The aid covers losses related to housing, vehicles, agricultural operations, and livestock. Applications for this support open on August 10 and will remain available for three months to facilitate recovery.
contextoradditionalinfo: A devastating wildfire in Castellón, Spain, has destroyed 9,600 hectares, causing significant damage to homes, livelihoods, and agricultural infrastructure. The regional government introduced this emergency measure to provide rapid financial relief and support the long-term economic and environmental recovery of the affected municipalities.
beneficiaries: residents, businesses, farmers, municipalities, irrigation communities
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Portugal has implemented a mandatory phase of its deposit return scheme for single-use beverage containers. From 10 August 2026, all eligible plastic bottles and metal cans up to three litres must display the Volta logo to be sold by retailers. Consumers are charged an additional €0.10 deposit per container, which is refundable upon return to authorized collection points. This measure aims to standardize the market and ensure all eligible packaging is integrated into the national recycling system.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of Portugal's strategy to meet European Union circular economy and waste reduction targets, specifically the EU Single-Use Plastics Directive. The directive requires Member States to achieve a 90 percent separate collection rate for plastic beverage bottles by 2029. The Volta system was introduced to boost recycling rates, reduce litter, and improve the quality of recyclable materials.

policydecision_details: Bulgaria is ending the mandatory dual pricing period for goods and services in both leva and euro on August 8, 2026. Starting August 9, 2026, merchants are required to display prices exclusively in euro. Businesses may voluntarily display the equivalent value in leva for reference, provided it is clearly marked as informational. Authorities will continue to monitor for unfair commercial practices and unjustified price increases to protect consumers during this transition.
contextoradditionalinfo: The dual price display requirement was initially introduced as a temporary measure to facilitate consumer adjustment to the euro and to prevent unfair price hikes during the currency changeover. As the country completes its transition to the single European currency, the government is phasing out these temporary transparency requirements while maintaining oversight through the Consumer Protection Commission.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Ecuadorian Ministry of Education has launched a USD 1.354 million resilience program to protect school infrastructure from the impacts of the El Niño phenomenon. The initiative prioritizes 264 educational institutions based on vulnerability and exposure criteria to ensure the continuity of educational services. Funding is split between physical infrastructure repairs, such as roofing and drainage, and the provision of flood-mitigation kits including pumps and generators. This program is part of the broader national education response plan, RESPONDEc-Educ, which integrates prevention, mitigation, and emergency response.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Government of Mozambique has approved a reform through Decrees no 40/2026 and no 41/2026 to simplify and accelerate the licensing of economic activities. The policy introduces digital procedures, such as the e-BAU platform and electronic signatures, to reduce administrative deadlines and paper documentation. A key measure includes issuing the Certificate of Mere Prior Communication within two hours and the Simplified License within one day. Additionally, micro-enterprises are now exempt from fees under the Mere Prior Communication regime. The reform aims to reduce costs and administrative barriers to encourage business formalization and investment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The reform was initiated to address excessive bureaucracy and high costs associated with starting and licensing businesses in Mozambique. By fostering a business environment based on trust and digitalization, the government seeks to boost entrepreneurship, attract investments, and facilitate the entry of young people into the formal market.
beneficiaries: micro-enterprises, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), entrepreneurs

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD) in Sofala is resuming food aid to the regions of Búzi, Nhamatanda, Muanza, and Dondo to support vulnerable families. Authorities are also distributing seeds and agricultural inputs to boost local production ahead of the anticipated El Niño-related drought. The initiative aims to reduce dependence on humanitarian aid by helping communities build food reserves. These measures are part of a broader effort to mitigate the impact of climate-related food insecurity in the province.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mozambique is facing significant food insecurity due to the combined effects of floods earlier in the year and the forecast of an El Niño-related drought. Approximately 250,000 people in Sofala are currently affected, and national estimates suggest over 3.5 million people across the country are facing acute food insecurity. The persistence of El Niño is expected to reduce rainfall and drive up food prices through 2026 and early 2027, threatening agricultural recovery.
decision_making_institution: National Institute for Disaster Risk Management and Reduction (INGD)
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Kenyan government has increased the producer price for locally grown wheat to KES 5,100 (USD 39) per 90-kilogram bag for the 2026 season. This adjustment represents an increase from the previous price of KES 4,750 (USD 36.6). The policy aims to improve farmers' earnings and encourage local production to reduce reliance on grain imports. The new price will be applied at designated government aggregation centres as part of a wheat mop-up exercise.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows consultations between the Agriculture and Food Authority, the Cereal Growers Association, and millers to balance the interests of producers and consumers. Wheat production has faced challenges due to adverse weather and a shift by farmers toward barley production in 2025. The government intends to prioritize locally produced grain and revitalize the wheat subsector through various support measures.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Cyprus has officially brought into force the legislation establishing the Cyprus Business Development Organisation (CBDO). The government has appointed a seven-member Board of Directors to lead the new entity. The primary mission of the CBDO is to improve access to financing for small and medium-sized enterprises, startups, and self-employed professionals. The organization is tasked with addressing identified financing gaps in the market to support business growth.
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized enterprises, startups, self-employed professionals

policydecision_details: The incoming Colombian government, has announced the full restoration of diplomatic and economic relations with Israel effective August 7, 2026. This policy includes the relocation of the Colombian embassy to Jerusalem and the initiation of bilateral processes to eliminate mutual tourist visa requirements. The decision reverses the diplomatic freeze and the termination of a bilateral free trade agreement enacted by the previous administration. Both nations have established a detailed roadmap to reappoint ambassadors and normalize bilateral cooperation.
