policydecision_details: Fiji and Australia have signed the Vuvale Union and the Ocean of Peace Alliance, establishing a comprehensive strategic partnership. This agreement secures $1.5 billion in new Australian investment to support Fiji's economic development and regional stability. The partnership focuses on key pillars including security, economic integration, and regionalism. It also includes an expansion of Australian development assistance to the Pacific, totaling AUD$2.2 billion.
decision_making_institution: Government of Fiji and Government of Australia

policydecision_details: Approved an interim land-use regulatory framework for the Union Territory. This policy allows for residential, commercial, industrial, or mixed-use development on land plots up to two kanals within Municipal Committee limits without requiring prior approval. The measure aims to streamline urban development and reduce bureaucratic hurdles for citizens and businesses. It will remain in effect until formal master plans and zonal development plans are notified.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address a significant regulatory gap caused by the absence of notified Master Plans and Zonal Development Plans in Ladakh. Currently, there are no Urban Development Authorities in the region to oversee these plans, which previously created uncertainty for construction and development activities. This interim framework provides necessary regulatory clarity while balancing developmental needs with environmental safeguards.
beneficiaries: residents of Ladakh, business owners, industrial developers

policydecision_details: Published a new Regulation on Plant Quarantine to update and replace the previous 2011 regulation. This new framework establishes updated plant health rules and official control procedures for the entry and exit of plants and plant products. The regulation aims to modernize the oversight of materials crossing national borders to prevent the spread of pests and diseases. It will officially enter into force on August 9, 2026, following a ninety-day transition period after its publication in the Official Gazette.
contextoradditionalinfo: The regulation was introduced to update existing plant health protocols and official control procedures, replacing the outdated 2011 Plant Quarantine Regulation to better manage risks associated with the international movement of plants and plant products.

policydecision_details: Announced a commitment to reduce public debt to below 80 percent of GDP. This fiscal policy decision aims to improve the country's macroeconomic stability. The commitment reflects a long-term strategy to manage national financial obligations. No specific implementation timeline or budgetary details were provided in the announcement.
contextoradditionalinfo: The announcement is part of Jordan's ongoing efforts to manage its national debt levels and ensure fiscal sustainability.

policydecision_details: Decided not to renew a water supply agreement with Jordan. This agreement previously provided the kingdom with additional water supplies at reduced prices. The decision follows a period of deteriorating diplomatic relations between the two countries. There are currently no expectations that the agreement will be signed or extended.
contextoradditionalinfo: The water deal was linked to the 1994 Wadi Araba peace treaty. Relations between Jordan and Israel have significantly worsened since the start of the conflict in Gaza in October 2023. Jordan has previously expressed frustration over the use of water as a political bargaining tool.

policydecision_details: Introduced the 'Customs Marine Bunkering Rules, 2026' to regulate customs processes for marine bunkering in Pakistan. These rules apply to operations at the Karachi Port Trust, Port Qasim Authority, and Gwadar Port Authority. All bunkering operations must be conducted electronically through the Pakistan Single Window (PSW) port community system. The regulation establishes a framework for authorized bunker operators and mandates compliance with MARPOL standards regarding fuel quality and sulphur content.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to modernize and formalize the regulatory framework for marine bunkering operations in Pakistan's major ports. By integrating these processes into the Pakistan Single Window, the government seeks to improve transparency, efficiency, and compliance with international maritime environmental standards.
beneficiaries: authorized bunker operators, shipping agents, vessel operators

policydecision_details: The Indonesian government has decided to scale back the rollout of its Red and White Cooperatives (KMP) program. The original target of 80,000 units has been reduced by half to 40,000 units for the October launch. The Finance Ministry emphasized that unnecessary augmentations to the program will be removed before implementation. The government is prioritizing the operational efficiency of the existing units before considering further expansion in the following year.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Indonesia and Singapore have established a new bilateral cooperation framework focused on clean energy transition. The agreement includes a carbon-credit framework under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and a comprehensive road map for cross-border electricity trade. These measures aim to facilitate commercial projects that align with Indonesia's National Energy Policy. The initiative seeks to leverage Indonesia's renewable energy potential to support regional energy security while fostering domestic industrial development.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Mines and Energy has granted a five-year geothermal exploration permit for the El Barranquero area, located between Samaná (Caldas) and Nariño (Antioquia). This permit authorizes a comprehensive exploration program, including geological, geophysical, and geochemical studies, as well as the drilling of a deep exploratory well. This initiative marks a significant step in incorporating geothermal energy into Colombia's national electricity matrix.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Spanish government has announced a State Fertilizer Plan to be implemented by the first quarter of 2027, aimed at increasing domestic production and reducing dependency on external supplies. This initiative is part of a broader mobilization of 1.1 billion euros in aid to the primary sector. The plan focuses on three main axes: promoting precision agriculture, ensuring strategic autonomy, and improving price transparency. Additionally, the government is currently distributing 665 million euros in direct aid to 425,000 beneficiaries to assist with fertilizer purchases.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the crisis in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which disrupted the supply of fertilizers. These inputs are considered essential for agricultural operations and food security. The government aims to mitigate the impact of these global uncertainties, including climate-related challenges like droughts and floods, on the viability of the agricultural sector and final food prices.

policydecision_details: Romania has published Order No. 828/2026, which introduces stricter transfer pricing documentation requirements for transactions with affiliated parties. The new framework mandates that large taxpayers prepare transfer pricing documentation annually by the corporate income tax filing deadline. This documentation must be submitted electronically via the Virtual Private Space (SPV) platform within 30 working days. The regulation aligns domestic rules with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, incorporating concepts like the Master File and detailed functional analysis. This shift transforms transfer pricing compliance from an audit-associated process into an annual obligation.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: Cabinet Decision No. (7) of 2026 prohibits the manufacturing, import, and circulation of single-use plastic bags with a thickness of less than 57 microns. This measure is designed to reduce the environmental impact of plastic waste. The decision is part of a broader national strategy to promote responsible production and consumption patterns. It requires the private sector to transition toward eco-friendly alternatives to support environmental sustainability goals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as part of the Kingdom of Bahrain’s growing commitment to strengthening environmental protection policies and preserving natural resources. It aligns with national development goals aimed at improving the quality of life and enhancing the country's attractiveness as a sustainable investment destination. The initiative is coordinated by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and the Supreme Council for Environment.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: Officially resumed international postal exchange services with Syria. This decision marks a restoration of communication and logistical channels between the two countries. The resumption of these services is expected to facilitate the movement of goods and correspondence. This measure is part of broader efforts to normalize cross-border interactions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The resumption of postal services follows a period of suspended relations and logistical disruptions between Jordan and Syria. Restoring these services is a step toward improving regional connectivity and trade facilitation.

policydecision_details: Launched a nationwide programme to identify, survey, title, and digitally register all public land. An initial budget of sh6b has been allocated for the current financial year to kickstart the process. The total cost of the initiative is estimated at sh100b, with a planned implementation timeline of five years. The first phase will prioritize urban centers where public land is under significant pressure from development and encroachment.
contextoradditionalinfo: Nearly three-quarters of government-owned land in Uganda remains untitled, leaving critical public assets such as schools, hospitals, roads, forests, and wetlands vulnerable to illegal occupation, fraud, and ownership disputes. The Uganda Land Commission reports that while government land accounts for 23% of the country's total land area, only 26.16% is formally documented. This lack of legal documentation has led to unclear boundaries and frequent, lengthy court disputes.

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has implemented a price reduction for 2,500 types of prescription drugs. This measure aims to increase the affordability of essential medications for the general public. The decision reflects a broader effort to manage healthcare costs within the country. The policy is currently in effect as of July 2026.

Confirmed that 15 vessels loaded with fertilizers are currently in transit to India. These vessels are reported to be crossing the Strait of Hormuz as part of the country's ongoing supply chain management. This movement ensures the continued availability of essential agricultural inputs for the domestic sector. The announcement serves as an update on the status of critical fertilizer imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Strait of Hormuz is a critical maritime chokepoint for global energy and commodity trade. Monitoring the transit of vessels through this region is essential for India to ensure the security and timely arrival of agricultural inputs like fertilizers, which are vital for national food production.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Extended the suspension of Perpetual Treasuries Limited (PTL) from operating as a Primary Dealer. This extension is for a period of six months. The measure is intended to allow for the continuation of ongoing investigations into the firm. PTL remains prohibited from conducting business activities during this period.
contextoradditionalinfo: The suspension is part of regulatory enforcement actions taken by the Central Bank of Sri Lanka under the Registered Stock and Securities Ordinance and the Local Treasury Bills Ordinance to ensure market integrity.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Chinese government has announced the cancellation of vehicle and vessel tax breaks for energy-saving vehicles and certain new energy vehicles (NEVs), effective January 1, 2027. Owners of affected vehicles, including plug-in hybrid electric vehicles and commercial NEVs, will be required to pay the annual tax starting next year. Pure electric passenger vehicles and fuel cell passenger vehicles remain exempt from this tax. This adjustment aims to promote tax equity and reflect the mature, market-driven stage of the NEV industry.
beneficiaries: owners of energy-saving vehicles, owners of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, owners of commercial new energy vehicles

policydecision_details: The Bilateral Investment Agreement (BIA) between India and Israel establishes a new framework for cross-border investment protection. It mandates that investors exhaust domestic legal remedies before pursuing international arbitration. The agreement preserves the sovereign right of both governments to regulate in areas such as taxation, public policy, and national security. It also introduces strict eligibility criteria for arbitrators and prohibits third-party funding to discourage speculative claims.
decision_making_institution: Government of India and Government of Israel

policydecision_details: Executed its third humanitarian aid flight to Venezuela to assist victims of the June 24 earthquakes. The shipment included 35 000 vaccines, various medicines, and 13 tons of cargo containing food and hygiene kits. This operation was coordinated by the Ministry of Health, the Undersecretary of the Interior, and the National Chamber of Pharmaceutical Laboratories. The aid is intended to address urgent health and nutritional needs in the affected areas.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following a series of earthquakes in Venezuela on June 24, the Chilean government initiated a series of humanitarian aid flights to support the affected population. This specific mission was a response to requests from the Venezuelan government for medical supplies and basic necessities to manage the emergency and the resulting health risks.

policydecision_details: Nine local governments have launched the Ring-fenced Agriculture Credit Guarantee Scheme (Agri-CGS) to improve access to formal credit for farmers and agricultural enterprises. The scheme introduces reforms to encourage banks to lend to borrowers lacking conventional collateral by providing a guarantee mechanism. The fund will mobilize USD 2 million in its initial phase, with contributions from the UN Joint Programme, the DCGF, and participating local governments. This initiative aims to reduce lending risks for financial institutions while expanding financing opportunities for underserved rural populations.
contextoradditionalinfo: Nepal's agriculture sector faces significant constraints, particularly limited access to affordable financing, which hinders growth and commercialization. In provinces like Karnali and Sudurpashchim, these challenges are compounded by food insecurity, climate-related shocks, and outmigration. The initiative is part of the UN Joint Programme on Innovative Financial Solutions for Local Food Systems Transformation in Nepal, designed to foster resilient local economies and inclusive development.
decision_making_institution: Nine local governments of Karnali, Sudurpashchim and Bagmati provinces
beneficiaries: smallholder farmers, women entrepreneurs, cooperatives, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs)

policydecision_details: Indonesia has introduced Minister of Manpower Regulation No. 11 of 2026 to update and strengthen the national labor inspection regime. This new regulation replaces the previous 2016 framework and revokes several sector-specific occupational safety and health (K3) provisions. Employers are now subject to more rigorous inspection procedures, which may occur without company representatives present. The regulation also emphasizes the use of the SIAPkerja digital platform for compliance and requires updated certifications for regulated industrial equipment.

The Federal Government of Germany has announced a comprehensive reform package consisting of 34 items aimed at stimulating the economy. The package includes tax relief measures totaling ten billion euros and a significant reduction in administrative red tape. It also proposes changes to employment contracts, including adjustments to dismissal protection and fixed-term contract regulations. The government intends for these measures to stabilize social security systems and foster economic growth.

The German coalition government has announced plans to require employees to provide a doctor's sick note on the first day of illness. This policy reverses a previous rule that only required a certificate after three days of absence. Additionally, the government intends to scrap the option of obtaining sick notes via telephone, a measure previously introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. The decision aims to reduce the high number of sick days taken by workers in Germany. The proposal is part of a broader set of labor and economic reforms.

The Portuguese Government declared a state of alert across mainland Portugal from July 3 to July 6, 2026, to mitigate the risk of rural fires. The measure imposes strict prohibitions on activities such as controlled burns, the use of machinery in forest areas, and access to designated forest tracks. Essential agricultural activities, including livestock feeding and irrigation, are permitted under specific conditions. Emergency services, including the GNR and PSP, have been placed on heightened readiness to manage potential fire outbreaks.

The Portuguese Parliament approved a bill to clarify the application of a reduced 6% VAT rate for urban rehabilitation projects. The measure confirms that the reduced rate applies to properties located in Urban Rehabilitation Areas (ARU) even if an Urban Rehabilitation Operation (ORU) has not been formally approved. This legislation includes retroactive effects dating back to 2008 to resolve ongoing disputes with the Tax Authority. The initiative aims to provide legal certainty for economic agents and families involved in urban rehabilitation.

Published its Monetary Policy Statement for the 2026-2027 period. This document provides a comprehensive update on the current state of the national economy. It outlines the Bank's outlook regarding inflation and economic growth. Furthermore, the statement details the specific actions the Bank intends to take to ensure price stability and foster sustainable economic growth. The publication serves as a communication tool to keep the public and stakeholders informed about future monetary expectations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Monetary Policy Statement is a regular institutional requirement to provide transparency and guidance on the Central Bank of Samoa's economic strategy and policy decisions.
beneficiaries: inflation and growth, sustainable economic growth

policydecision_details: Signed a protocol updating bilateral double taxation agreement with Sweden, bringing the treaty into line with OECD international tax standards and strengthening cooperation on tax transparency and the exchange of information.

Released Rs 500 million (USD 3.65 million) to provide financial compensation to poultry farmers affected by a widespread bird flu outbreak. Under the Bird Flu Disease Control (Fourth Amendment) Regulation, 2074, eligible farmers can receive up to 75 percent of their verified losses. The funds were transferred to the Department of Livestock Services to expedite payments for destroyed birds, eggs, and feed. Additionally, the government has intensified biosecurity measures and warned against the sale of infected poultry to prevent further spread and protect public health.
contextoradditionalinfo: An outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza has spread across 11 districts in Nepal, resulting in the destruction of approximately 700,000 birds, 1.1 million eggs, and 300,000 kilograms of poultry feed. Total financial losses for the poultry sector are estimated at Rs 700 million. The government intervention aims to mitigate the economic impact on farmers and contain the virus, which has been linked to infected wild birds and improper disposal of dead poultry.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment

policydecision_details: Announced a significant increase in the public service wage bill by Shs1.09 trillion (USD 306 million). This measure involves the enhancement of salaries for specific categories of public servants, including Arts Teachers, Head Teachers, Assistant Commissioners, Town Clerks, and Deputy Chief Administrative Officers. The salary adjustments are effective for the 2026/2027 Financial Year. This decision aims to improve service delivery excellence across the public sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the government's broader effort to enhance public service delivery and adjust compensation for key administrative and educational staff within the public sector.
beneficiaries: Arts Teachers, Head Teachers, Assistant Commissioners, Town Clerks, Deputy Chief Administrative Officers

policydecision_details: Approved a loan agreement with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for EUR 423.8 million to support a development policy for employment and green growth.

The President of Uzbekistan signed a decree to increase national fish production to 500,000 tons by 2027 through intensive rearing technologies and the development of cold-water fish farming. The policy establishes a Fish Farming Development Center and a dedicated support fund to manage the industry and provide financial assistance. It introduces electronic auctions for leasing water bodies and launches the 'e-baliq' platform to monitor production data. Additionally, the government will provide subsidies for equipment, pedigree fish imports, and expert wages, alongside new educational programs for aquaculture specialists.

The Government of Uzbekistan has issued a resolution to implement a hunting ban on rare and highly endangered wild animal species from 1 August 2026 to 1 January 2028. The ban includes species such as the snow leopard, saiga antelope, and various birds, though it excludes animals raised on farms or those caught for scientific and medical purposes. Additionally, the government mandates the annual stocking of at least 15 tonnes of fingerlings in rivers flowing through central cities from 2026 to 2030. This measure aims to compensate for losses in the animal world and protect biodiversity. No hunting quotas will be allocated for the prohibited species during the ban period.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader initiative to compensate for losses of the animal world and ensure the protection of rare and highly endangered wild animals in Uzbekistan.

policydecision_details: The Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis has approved a draft law amending the national legislation on veterinary medicine. The bill establishes core principles for state policy in the veterinary sector and clarifies the powers of the Food Safety Committee. It introduces improved legal norms for the production, processing, storage, transportation, and sale of products subject to veterinary control. Furthermore, the legislation aligns national veterinary standards with international requirements and World Trade Organization rules.
decision_making_institution: Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis
beneficiaries: livestock producers, food processors, veterinary services

policydecision_details: Bangladesh Bank has introduced Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) to allow Authorized Dealers to help importers hedge interest rate risks associated with suppliers' and buyers' credit in foreign currency. The policy permits importers to fix interest rates for future periods to manage volatility in floating rate credits. Authorized Dealers are required to cover these transactions on a back-to-back basis to prevent unmitigated market risk on their balance sheets. The regulation includes strict documentation, mark-to-market valuation requirements, and limits on the total notional outstanding relative to foreign exchange inflows.

The European Commission has approved the sixth disbursement of USD 8 billion to Spain under the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Mechanism. This funding follows the successful achievement of 73 milestones and targets, including significant legislative reforms and investments. Key initiatives supported by this disbursement include the establishment of over fifty support centers for victims of sexual violence and the strengthening of the Minimum Basic Income. These measures aim to enhance social protection, remove barriers to employability, and facilitate entry into the labor market.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The European Commission has allocated USD 92 million to Portugal for energy efficiency programs in public buildings. Specifically, USD 76 million will fund an integrated energy modernization program for the Judiciary Police, while USD16 million will support sustainable building initiatives for the National Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences. These funds are part of a broader package from the EU Modernization Fund. The initiative aims to modernize energy systems, reduce fossil fuel imports, and meet climate goals.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Portuguese government is expanding the E-Home programme to include a new phase that integrates support for energy-efficient household appliances and photovoltaic systems. This initiative aims to help families reduce energy costs and accelerate the transition to cleaner energy sources. Additionally, the government is launching a USD 1.8 billion Social Climate Fund to support vulnerable households and small and medium-sized enterprises in low-density regions. The fund will also finance sustainable transport initiatives, including electric buses and innovative mobility solutions, with project financing expected to begin in mid-2027.
contextoradditionalinfo: The expansion of the E-Home programme and the creation of the Social Climate Fund are part of Portugal's broader strategy to address energy poverty and climate change. The Environmental Fund has faced financial pressure due to recent storm-related spending and global economic crises, prompting the government to integrate solar and appliance incentives into a single, more efficient scheme. Portugal has already made progress in improving energy efficiency through the Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR), which has supported the rehabilitation of 85,000 apartments.
beneficiaries: vulnerable households, small and medium-sized enterprises
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Approved the establishment of the Higher Joint Lebanese-Syrian Commission to formalize institutional coordination between the two countries. This commission serves as a top-level mechanism for consultation and cooperation across various sectors, including economic, commercial, and investment affairs. The agreement was signed by Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and Syrian Foreign Minister Assaad al-Shaibani. The mandate covers a broad range of areas such as energy, transport, and infrastructure, aiming to strengthen bilateral relations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision aims to formalize a new institutional framework for coordination between Lebanon and Syria. It follows a meeting at the Grand Serail where the government sought to establish a structured approach to bilateral cooperation, covering political, diplomatic, and economic sectors.

policydecision_details: Ratified the 20th amendment to the Maldives Export-Import Act. The amendment establishes a new import duty structure for cigarettes, bidis, and heated tobacco consumables, set at MVR 4 flat plus a 30 percent ad valorem duty. Conversely, the policy provides an exemption from import duties for smoking cessation products such as nicotine gum and patches. The amendment took effect immediately upon its ratification and publication in the Government Gazette.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as part of the 20th amendment to the Export-Import Act (Law Number 79/31) to regulate the taxation of tobacco products in the Maldives.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Issued a Sales Tax General Order mandating the clear, prominent, and indelible display of retail prices and sales tax amounts on all goods specified in the Third Schedule of the Sales Tax Act, 1990. Manufacturers and importers must ensure that this information is not obscured by designs, monograms, or other materials. The order specifies that font size and color must contrast with the background to ensure readability for consumers. Failure to comply with these requirements will result in legal action under the Sales Tax Act, 1990.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Federal Board of Revenue observed that in many cases, the retail price on goods listed in the Third Schedule was either missing, not clearly visible, or obscured by packaging designs, making it difficult for consumers and tax authorities to ascertain the correct price and applicable sales tax.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
additionalcommodities: Fruits and derived products|Milk and dairy products|Poultry meat and eggs|Tea|Cereals and cereal products

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the Technological University of Panama (UTP) have signed a Framework Cooperation Agreement to foster joint initiatives in academic, scientific, technical, and cultural fields. This partnership aims to strengthen institutional capacities, promote innovation, and enhance the training of human talent within the State. The agreement includes specific programs for the professional development of public servants and provides opportunities for students to engage in internships and projects. Furthermore, the collaboration focuses on integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, into fiscal management and economic analysis processes.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement was established to address the need for institutional modernization and the development of human capital in the public sector. By leveraging the UTP's expertise in engineering, science, and technology, the MEF seeks to improve its analytical processes and economic projections. This initiative reflects a strategic effort to align public administration with advancements in STEM fields and digital transformation.
beneficiaries: public servants, students, Technological University of Panama (UTP)

policydecision_details: Established a strategic alliance with IDB Invest to mobilize up to USD 01 000 million in private investment. This initiative aims to boost economic growth and job creation by providing financing and technical support to private sector projects. The strategy focuses on high-potential sectors, including agribusiness, energy, and infrastructure, with a specific priority on supporting micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The program operates through independent project evaluation by IDB Invest and does not involve public debt or sovereign guarantees.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the National Government's broader efforts to stimulate the Panamanian economy, attract private investment, and strengthen sectors with high growth potential to generate new employment opportunities for citizens.
decision_making_institution: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
commodity1: Others meat or animal derived products

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced an expansion of financial support for the cotton and textile sector. This initiative includes the provision of new subsidies to boost production capacity. Additionally, the policy introduces VAT incentives to reduce the tax burden on industry participants. These measures are designed to strengthen the competitiveness of the national textile value chain.

Turkmenistan has commissioned new modern water management facilities in the Gokdepe etrap of Ahal velayat and the city of Ashgabat. These facilities include advanced water-lifting stations and hydraulic structures equipped with digital, automated control systems and solar power integration. The infrastructure is designed to ensure an uninterrupted water supply for over 6,000 hectares of agricultural land and to improve domestic drinking water access for the capital. This initiative reflects the government's commitment to modernizing the water sector through innovative technologies and sustainable resource management.
beneficiaries: agricultural producers, rural population, urban population

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan is maintaining duty-free fuel imports and continuing price control measures to ensure market stability. The government is providing partial compensation to fuel and lubricant importers to curb domestic price increases. The Antimonopoly Regulation Service is actively monitoring compliance with established maximum retail prices for gasoline and diesel. Additionally, the government is seeking alternative suppliers and logistics routes to reduce dependence on existing supply chains.
beneficiaries: fuel and lubricant importers, domestic consumers
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development has issued detailed guidelines for the granting, payment, and return of financial assistance under the Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy 2023-2027. Specifically, these guidelines pertain to intervention I.10.3, which focuses on investments aimed at preventing the spread of African Swine Fever (ASF). The regulations define the conditions for aid, selection criteria, and payment procedures for eligible farmers. These guidelines become effective on July 1, 2026, and apply to new applications submitted from that date forward.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

policydecision_details: The Bulgarian government has approved the 2026–2028 Public Debt Management Strategy to manage national debt and refinance outstanding obligations. The strategy outlines refinancing requirements ofUSD 1.6 billion in 2026, USD 2 billion in 2027, USD 3 billion in 2028. New debt financing will also support state budget deficits and provide liquidity for state-owned enterprises across various sectors, including agriculture and water management. Additionally, the government confirmed an increase in the minimum monthly wage to EUR 620.20 effective January 1, 2026.
budget: USD 1.6 billion in 2026, USD 2 billion in 2027, USD 3 billion in 2028

policydecision_details: The Deputy Director of Management and Management of Protected Areas of National Natural Parks of Colombia has issued a resolution to officially register the 'El Cedrito' property as a Natural Reserve of Civil Society. This administrative act formalizes the conservation status of the area, recognizing it as a site that preserves a sample of a natural ecosystem. The decision is based on the legal authority granted by Decree 3572 of 2011 and Law 99 of 1993. The registration ensures the property is managed under principles of sustainability in the use of natural resources.

France has introduced an additional one to two months of paid parental leave for both mothers and fathers. This new policy allows parents to receive 70% of their net salary during the first month and 60% during the second month of this extra leave. The provisions apply to parents of children born on or after January 1, 2026, and also include adoptive parents. This measure aims to provide additional support to families beyond existing maternity and paternity leave entitlements.

The Central Bank of Paraguay has implemented a reduction in commission rates for electronic payment transactions. The maximum commission for credit card transactions is lowered from 4% to 3%, while the cap for debit card transactions is reduced from 3% to 2%. This measure applies to all payment operators and card issuers providing intermediation services. The policy aims to lower the cost of accepting electronic payments for businesses and encourage the use of digital payment methods. The regulation is enacted under the authority of Law No. 5.476/15 to ensure transparency and user protection.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Croatia has introduced mandatory country-of-origin labelling for all fresh produce sold at markets. Effective from 1 July 2026, sellers are required to clearly display the country of origin alongside the price for fruit, vegetables, and other fresh produce. This measure aims to increase transparency and assist consumers in making informed purchasing decisions. Additionally, the government has relaxed cosmetic standards for fresh domestic produce to help reduce food waste.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The National Coalition for Caymanians (NCFC) approved a supplementary budget appropriation of USD 160 million to address emerging capital expenditure needs. The largest portion of this funding, USD 72 million, was allocated to the Ministry of Planning, Lands, Agriculture, Housing and Infrastructure to cover expenditures including road works, land acquisitions, and port upgrades. Additionally, USD 59 million was directed to the Ministry of Education for school infrastructure projects. The government stated that this spending is supported by higher-than-projected revenue performance from the financial services sector.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Issued amendments to the operational guidelines for the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) - Niryat Disha. The policy introduces a differentiated financial assistance structure for MSMEs, providing up to 95 percent reimbursement for Micro and Small Enterprises and 80 percent for Medium Enterprises, with increased cumulative caps. It also mandates a two-stage reimbursement claim process linked to certification and actual export realization. These changes aim to provide operational clarity and support for MSMEs involved in international value chains. The list of eligible testing, inspections, and certifications has been updated to be dynamic and subject to periodic review.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is a continuation of the Export Promotion Mission (EPM) - Niryat Disha, building upon Trade Notice No. 26/2025-26. It is designed to enhance the compliance and accreditation capabilities of Indian MSMEs to facilitate their participation in global trade.
budget: ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh per IEC per financial year
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: The Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Bill, 2026, aims to formally recognize women farmers through the issuance of official certificates. This recognition is designed to facilitate their access to various government welfare schemes, programs, and credit facilities. The bill mandates the establishment of a dedicated Women Farmers Database, a State Fund, an Empowerment Cell, and an Empowerment Council. These institutional mechanisms are intended to support women's participation in agriculture and improve their socio-economic status. The legislation covers a wide range of agricultural activities, including cultivation, animal husbandry, and agro-forestry.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the significant role women play in the rural agricultural sector of Maharashtra. Recognizing that women's participation is increasing, the government identified the need for formal empowerment to ensure future agricultural growth and sustainability. The bill also highlights the importance of women's involvement in protecting food security amidst the challenges of climate change.

policydecision_details: Issued a public notification regarding updates to the Road Safety and Transport Rules. The announcement introduces a One-Time Mass Vehicle Ownership service for the general public. The BCTA has provided contact information for both transport and construction services to facilitate public inquiries.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy serves as an administrative update to transport regulations and vehicle ownership processes in Bhutan, managed by the BCTA.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Extended the One-Time Mass Vehicle Ownership Transfer Facilitation Initiative. This extension provides vehicle owners with additional time to complete ownership transfers. After this final deadline, all transfers must strictly adhere to the regular procedures under the Road Safety and Transport Regulations. Owners are encouraged to visit BCTA offices to finalize their transfers before the cutoff date.
contextoradditionalinfo: The extension was granted to accommodate vehicle owners following service disruptions caused by the recent integration of the e Ra LIS–BIRMS system.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Revised the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) on the export of petrol, diesel, and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). The export duty is set at Rs 4 (USD 0.05) per litre for petrol, Rs 8.5 (USD 0.10) per litre for diesel, and Rs 7.5 (USD 0.09) per litre for ATF. The policy also expands the list of countries exempted from these export duties to include Mauritius and the Maldives. Domestic fuel taxes remain unchanged to protect local consumers from direct price impacts.
contextoradditionalinfo: The measure is part of a fortnightly review of export levies introduced on 27 March 2026. The primary objective is to ensure the domestic availability of petroleum products by discouraging exports during the ongoing West Asia crisis.
commodity2: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: Announced updated, increased prices for LPG refills across Saudi Arabia. The new pricing structure sets an 11-kilogram cylinder at SR 37 (USD 9.87) and a 5-kilogram cylinder at SR 16.82 (USD 4.49). Additionally, the price for refilling central gas tanks has been raised to SR 1.69 (USD 0.45) per liter. These prices are inclusive of VAT and transportation costs and apply nationwide.
contextoradditionalinfo: The revised rates replace the previous unified LPG pricing structure that was introduced in January 2026 to standardize costs across all regions of the Kingdom. The adjustment reflects a change in the national pricing strategy for energy products.

policydecision_details: Initiated early preparations for the 2026/2027 farming season. A key component of this preparation is the commencement of training for agro-dealers involved in the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP). This training aims to streamline the distribution of agricultural inputs to farmers. By starting early, the government intends to ensure that necessary resources are available in time for the upcoming planting season.
contextoradditionalinfo: In Zambia, agriculture is a critical sector that supports industrial raw material production, export growth, rural employment, and national nutrition standards. The government is prioritizing early preparation to ensure the efficiency of the FISP and to maintain agricultural productivity.

policydecision_details: Issued Circular Standing Instruction No. 6 regarding the salary structure for the financial year 2026/2027. This policy outlines the compensation framework for civil servants in Uganda for the specified fiscal period. It serves as the official administrative guidance for public sector remuneration. The instruction is part of the government's routine fiscal planning and human resource management for the public service.
contextoradditionalinfo: This circular is a standard administrative procedure issued by the Ministry of Public Service to define salary scales and structures for government employees for the upcoming financial year 2026/2027.

policydecision_details: Parliament Watch Uganda is an initiative focused on monitoring parliamentary processes. Its primary objective is to enhance the transparency, responsiveness, and accountability of the Ugandan Parliament. By providing information on legislative activities, it aims to improve public oversight of government functions. This initiative serves as a platform for civic engagement rather than a specific agricultural policy measure.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative was established to address the need for greater public access to information regarding parliamentary proceedings and to foster a more accountable legislative environment in Uganda.

policydecision_details: Launched the re-engineered Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) 2.0 system. This platform will fully digitize the procurement cycle across all government procuring and disposing entities, including local governments. The system introduces enhanced features such as a Central Supplier Platform for one-time registration, e-contract management, and real-time reporting dashboards. By automating processes, the government aims to improve efficiency, transparency, and accountability while reducing manual handling of documents. This initiative is supported by the amended PPDA Act (2021) and recent procurement guidelines.
contextoradditionalinfo: The e-GP system was initially introduced in 2021 to address inefficiencies and corruption in public procurement. Following a successful pilot phase that expanded to 36 entities by 2025, the government decided to scale the system nationally to ensure standardized, traceable, and transparent procurement transactions across the entire public sector.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Approved the end-user electricity tariffs for the third quarter of 2026, effective from July to September. The decision establishes specific tariff rates for various consumer categories, including domestic, commercial, and industrial users. The Authority has maintained the Lifeline Tariff for low-consumption domestic customers and the Cooking Tariff to encourage the adoption of electric cooking. This adjustment reflects changes in macroeconomic factors such as currency depreciation, international oil prices, and inflation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The tariff adjustment was necessitated by a 4.22% depreciation of the Uganda Shilling against the US Dollar, rising international oil prices affecting thermal power plant costs, and an increase in the core Consumer Price Index. These factors collectively raised the operating costs for electricity generation, transmission, and distribution companies. The review also accounts for changes in the energy generation mix, which saw increased dispatch from more cost-effective large hydro power plants.
beneficiaries: Domestic Consumers, Commercial Consumers, Industrial Consumers, Public Amenities
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) has invested USD 50 million in a USD 200 million bond issued by China Education Group Holdings Limited (CEG). This investment supports the campus expansion of the Guangzhou College of Applied Science and Technology in Zhaoqing New City. The project aims to address the growing demand for industry-oriented skills training and contribute to sustainable urban development. By acting as an anchor investor, the AIIB successfully mobilized additional private capital from various international financial institutions.
beneficiaries: students, higher education institutions, vocational education sector

policydecision_details: Ukraine's state budget has received USD 3.35 billion under the First Ukraine Jobs and Private Sector Growth Development Policy Operation, implemented jointly with the World Bank. The funds will be used to support macroeconomic stability and finance priority state budget expenditures under martial law.

The Indonesian government issued Minister of Finance Regulation No. 43 of 2026 (PMK-43) to provide a government-borne VAT (VAT DTP) incentive for economy-class domestic commercial airline tickets. The government will cover 100% of the VAT payable on the base fare and fuel surcharge for tickets purchased between June 22 and July 5, 2026. This measure is designed to stimulate the economy during the school holiday period. Airlines are required to report these transactions as services benefiting from the VAT DTP facility in their monthly VAT returns.

The Government of Malawi has secured US$130 million in grant funding from the International Development Association (IDA) to support two major projects. The Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project receives US$80 million to improve financial management and service delivery at the local council level. The Transforming High-Potential Resilient Value Chains Project receives US$50 million to boost export sectors through improved access to finance, trade policy reforms, and climate resilience. The legislation also authorizes the establishment of a Partial Credit Guarantee Fund to facilitate lending to export-oriented firms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The funding aims to address weaknesses in local governance and limited export capacity in Malawi. By strengthening financial management at the council level and providing credit guarantees and advisory services to export-oriented businesses, the government seeks to diversify the economy and reduce vulnerability to market and climate-related shocks.
beneficiaries: district and municipal councils, export-oriented firms, businesses in export value chains

policydecision_details: The Government of the Slovak Republic approved a draft Double Taxation Agreement with the Arab Republic of Egypt via Resolution No. 252/2026. This agreement aims to prevent tax evasion and avoidance while reducing the risk of double taxation for organizations and mobile employees. Once signed and ratified, the treaty will provide greater clarity on tax residence and withholding requirements. It is expected to simplify payroll administration and assignment cost management for businesses operating between the two countries.
beneficiaries: organizations with cross-border activity, globally mobile employees

policydecision_details: The Regional Directorate for Environmental Protection in Katowice has officially established two new nature reserves, Bogdaniec and Psi Nos, in the Silesian Voivodeship. These reserves cover a combined area of approximately 220 hectares, protecting valuable Jurassic forest ecosystems and limestone hills. The creation of these sites brings the total number of nature reserves in the region to 70. This measure aims to preserve unique habitats and biodiversity within the Krakow-Częstochowa Upland for the long term.
decision_making_institution: Regionalna Dyrekcja Ochrony Środowiska w Katowicach

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development, in coordination with the National Environmental License Authority (Anla), has adopted 17 measures to mitigate the impacts of the El Niño phenomenon. These actions include strengthening water resource management, prioritizing human and agricultural supply, and implementing early warning systems for forest fires. Additionally, Anla has issued seven guidelines for environmental license holders to review contingency plans and adjust water-saving programs. These measures aim to protect ecosystems, wildlife, and food security during the expected climate variability period. The government is acting preventively to enhance the country's response capacity against the high probability of the El Niño phenomenon.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
beneficiaries: territorial entities, holders of environmental licenses, communities
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Foreigners in Slovakia will no longer be charged more for fuel than locals from Friday, Economy Minister Denisa Sakova announced on Wednesday, ending a controversial price regulation that had drawn criticism from the European Commission.

Announced the review of a proposed TBH 400 billion (about USD 11 billion) loan decree aimed at mitigating the economic impact of Middle East tensions. The funds would support the “Thai Chuay Thai Plus” stimulus programme, scheduled to run from June through September this year.

Authorised an investment of USD 14.6 million to distribute nearly 342 000 bags of fertiliser and seeds to paesant families. The initiative aimes to strengthen national food production and ensure continuity in support programs. the government will purchase 181 930 bags of NPK 12-24-12 fertilizer and 160 000 bags of ammonium sulfate. This specific procurement is valued at 11 billion kwanzas, (EUR 10.3 million), and includes specialized services for production support, imported seeds, and agricultural tools.
The Islamic Development Bank has approved a USD 59.28 million rural electrification plan in Mauritania.

Implemented a series of emergency measures to protect the economy and supply chains amid the Middle East crisis. Key actions include introducing subsidies on animal feed to boost local meat production and instructing the Seychelles Trading Company to purchase all additional local produce from farmers. The government is also increasing fuel prices at the pump while maintaining electricity tariffs to manage consumption. Furthermore, businesses are receiving relief through targeted tax breaks, rent reductions, and flexible loan arrangements to safeguard employment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the Middle East crisis, which has negatively impacted global markets, air connectivity, and tourism in Seychelles. The government aims to mitigate the resulting economic instability, potential supply chain disruptions, and rising costs of living by strengthening local production and securing essential commodity reserves.
beneficiaries: farmers, fishers, businesses, public service employees

policydecision_details: Issued new guidelines aimed at protecting policyholders and their investments in the event of insurance or reinsurance companies going under or liquidated.
Inaugurated the first petroleum testing laboratory, develoed to improve fuel quality control, reduce import delays ans strengthened downstream oversight.

Poland and Sweden have signed a letter of intent to strengthen their strategic partnership in civil protection and civil defence. The agreement focuses on four key areas: security against drone threats, management of strategic reserves, social resilience, and coastal security. This collaboration builds upon existing joint activities and aims to enhance operational initiatives between the two nations. The initiative is supported by a significant national investment in civil protection programs for 2025-2026.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of the Interior and Administration

policydecision_details: The Bulgarian Parliament approved the 2026 National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) budget at the first reading. The budget sets total revenue and transfers at USD 5.7 billion, with expenditure increasing by 8.5% compared to 2025. The plan allocates significant funding for hospital and outpatient care services. The health insurance contribution rate remains fixed at 8%, maintaining the existing split between employers and employees.

The Kenyan Ministry of Health has signed a Cooperation Framework with the Beginnings Fund to invest USD 80 million over five years to reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths. The initiative supports the Every Woman Every Newborn Everywhere (EWENE) Acceleration Plan and the country's 90-90-80-80 health targets. Key investments will focus on 21 high-burden counties, improving health infrastructure, expanding the workforce, and enhancing the availability of lifesaving medicines and medical technologies. The program aims to benefit nearly six million women and newborns by 2030 while strengthening the national health system.

The Honduran government has announced an unprecedented investment of USD 75 million to strengthen the national coffee sector. The funds are designated for marketing, working capital, plantation renewal, farm maintenance, and productivity incentives. Additionally, USD 22 million are allocated for social investment in coffee-growing communities to support producing families. Furthermore, USD 40 million in microcredits will be channeled through BANADESA, specifically targeting rural women and youth to foster social inclusion.
contextoradditionalinfo: Coffee is a primary economic engine for Honduras, and the government aims to consolidate it as the main agricultural export product. The initiative seeks to boost productivity and generate over 2,000 million dollars in foreign currency this year while promoting sustainable development and social inclusion in the rural countryside.
beneficiaries: coffee producers, rural women, youth, coffee-growing communities

policydecision_details: Decree No. 216 introduces comprehensive measures to stimulate socio-economic development in specific districts of the Mogilev and Vitebsk regions until 2030. The policy provides for state-funded transfers to reimburse up to 35% of capital costs for approved investment projects. It also facilitates technical re-equipment of organizations through co-financing of equipment purchases from republican and regional budgets. Additionally, the decree allows agricultural organizations to purchase cattle heifers using funds from the republican budget. These measures aim to foster the creation of new enterprises and production facilities in the targeted regions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to provide an additional impetus to the socio-economic development of the south-eastern region of the Mogilev region and the Poozerie region in the Vitebsk region. These areas require targeted support to improve economic conditions, encourage investment, and modernize production facilities. The decree builds upon previous regional development initiatives to ensure long-term growth and stability in these specific territories.
decision_making_institution: President of the Republic of Belarus
beneficiaries: agricultural organizations, enterprises in south-eastern Mogilev region, enterprises in Poozerie region

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The President of Colombia has issued a decree to regulate articles 21 and 21-1 of Law 1715 of 2014, as modified by Law 2099 of 2021. This regulatory framework specifically addresses the development of activities for the generation of electrical energy through geothermal sources. The decree integrates these provisions into the Sole Regulatory Decree of the Administrative Sector of Mines and Energy (Decree 1073 of 2015). It aims to establish clear guidelines for the economic use of geothermal resources as a renewable energy source.
decision_making_institution: President of the Republic of Colombia
beneficiaries: the economic use, the exercise of, the energy transition
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: The National Authority of Environmental Licenses (ANLA) issued Resolution N° 00321 to impose additional environmental obligations on the company HOLCIM COLOMBIA S. A. These requirements pertain to the Environmental Management and Restoration Plan for limestone extraction activities in the municipalities of Tibasosa, Nobsa, Corrales, and Busbanzá. The decision follows a series of previous monitoring and control actions conducted by the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development since 2004. The measure aims to ensure compliance with environmental standards in the company's mining concessions.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
